title: Decomposing Earth Embeddings with Sparse Autoencoders
summary: Sparse autoencoders decomposed AlphaEarth and Tessera Earth-observation embeddings into sparse features. At matched sparsity they reconstructed the embeddings better than PCA, ICA, NMF and other baselines. Some feature-specificity measures also appeared with a frozen random decoder, so the result supports learned reconstruction quality rather than new geographic discoveries.
ai_technology: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) applied to AlphaEarth and Tessera embeddings
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: At matched sparsity, trained SAEs reconstructed AlphaEarth and Tessera embeddings better than the tested baselines. Sparse features aligned with fewer reference concept groups and carried more variance at fine spatial scales; a frozen random decoder shared those latter properties.
evidence.unknown: This is a representation evaluation; application demonstrations are not yet reliable enough for practical use, and no newly established geographic classes are claimed.
evidence.ai_role: Sparse autoencoders transform dense Earth-observation embeddings into sparse feature codes; evaluation compared reconstruction, concept alignment and spatial scale against PCA, ICA, NMF and frozen random-decoder baselines.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
